To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the breakdown of the quantum hall effect in GaAs/AlxGa1-xAs heterostructures occurs in at least two states with different longitudinal resistances, (ii) these two states can coexist at the same magnetic field and current, and (iii) the time the current carrier stays in the dissipative state increases with the current.
the QHE breakdown is a bistable process, which is caused by the current carriers.

the current-induced switching between the two states of the QHE occurs in a statistical manner with a time distribution of the longitudinal voltage and a characteristic time rho dis that depends on the current, magnetic field, and temperature.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the current-induced breakdown behaviour of the integer QHE in a two-dimensional electron gas in GaAs/Al0.3Ga0.7As heterostructures.
the breakdown behaviour of two-dimensional electron systems in GaAs/AlxGa1-xAs heterostructures.
the breakdown behavior of the quantum Hall Effect (QHE) at very low temperatures (T approx. 100 mK).
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the results can be understood within the framework of the model of a current-induced depopulation of the lowest Landau level, which leads to a breakdown of the QH effect, if the current carriers are able to escape from the constriction.
the current-induced QHE breakdown is not a simple one-step process, but rather a complex phenomenon involving at least two states of the system.
the current-induced QHE breakdown is a bistable process.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the breakdown behaviour of a sample with a constriction is determined by the interplay of several different effects.

we have observed a bistable behaviour of a quantum Hall system, which is in agreement with the predictions of the model by Chalker and Coddington, but not in agreement with the prediction of the model by Koulakov et al. (1995).
a current-induced breakdown of a non-dissipationless quantum Hall state is a bistable process.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the current-induced transition from the QHE into the resistive state is a first-order phase transition.
the current-induced switching behaviour is a general feature of the breakdown of the QHA and not restricted to samples with constrictions.
the breakdown behaviour of GaAs heterostructures can be understood as the switching between two different states of current carriers.
